description: We are a motivated team from Agadir specialized in Full Stack Web Development, passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation. We aim to create an engaging solution for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. We welcome motivated members with skills in AI/ML, game development, UI/UX, graphic design, space science, or multimedia.
summary: Space Rush is a browser game for kids aged 7-12 that teaches how astronauts survive on the Moon. Kids don't answer quizzes: they play it. Across 10 missions, from packing the rocket on Earth to running a Moon base for 12 days, children run, carry, fix and plan while balancing air, water, power, food and radiation. Every choice has a consequence they can feel, like a solar storm that hits while they're still outside. After each mission, RIO the robot explains what happened and why, so kids learn real trade-offs by living them. The storms and radiation levels come from real NASA data, which makes Moon survival concrete and memorable for young learners.
details:
WHAT IT IS: Space Rush is a path of 10 missions for kids aged 7-12, like a language-learning app, but every level is a mission, not a lesson. The child goes from packing a rocket on Earth to running a Moon base for 12 days.

HOW IT WORKS: There are two kinds of missions. In SURVIVE missions (real time), the child moves an astronaut around the base: pack 6 cargo spaces in 75 seconds, collect power cells before night, mine ice for water, fix failing systems, and build a shelter wall before a solar storm hits. In PLAN missions (day by day), the child plans the base with 4 moves per day and watches the simulation play out: power, air, water, food, radiation and crew health. Choices carry forward: forgetting the toolbox means a leak during the trip.

WHY IT TEACHES: Failing is safe. After each mission, RIO the robot gives a report with a chart of the resources over time and explains the key moments in one sentence each (for example: 'You were outside for 9 seconds of the storm. That one extra bag was not worth it!'). Then the child tries again with a better plan. Kids learn real engineering trade-offs because they feel them, not because they memorise them.

DESIGNED FOR KIDS: RIO reads every instruction aloud, so slow readers can play. The look is a cartoon storybook. All game values are labelled as simplified game units, and real facts are shown separately with their source. Child safety: the game only stores a first name on the device. No account, no chat, no tracking, no ads.

TOOLS: HTML, CSS and JavaScript; Canvas 2D (all art is drawn by code, no image files); Web Speech API for RIO's voice (the browser's built-in text-to-speech); Web Audio API for sound effects. Works on phones and computers, no install, runs offline.

USE OF AI: We used Claude (by Anthropic), an AI assistant, to write the game's code (including the code that draws all the art), to lay out our pitch deck and to help write texts. Our team chose the idea, the age group, the missions, the design and the learning goals, tested the game and decided every change. RIO's voice is generated by the browser's text-to-speech. No AI-generated images and no NASA branding are used.
